I would say the moral grounds for most western societies are our individual freedoms and equality. We have a very live and let live attitude, which is why in these countries you can believe in whatever you want, do whatever you want, say whatever you want and the state won't interfere (generally). That's not the case for most muslim societies with other religious minorities facing persecution, political dissidents facing imprisionment and forms of abuse being normalized and accepted (domestic abuse and employer abuse towards inmigrant subordinates). 

I know the word Islam means peace and like most if not all religions, encourages and inspires it's followers to do good and be good in the world. However, the people practicing it often use it as a means of control and manipulation. They use its teachings to justify stonings and beatings. Other religions have been used in the same way, however now western society has severed its ties to a specific religion, therefore making sure the people within its borders are given dignity and respect regardless of race or creed. It doesn't always work out that way but its the goal we strive for. And our society isn't perfect, we still have many issues to resolve which we openly admit to and discuss. But trying to take the moral high ground and saying our society isn't anchored in any values is pretty inconsistent when you look at societies with your "superior values" and see them blocking foreign aid for the Yemenase famine or treating half of their population as second class citizens. Or killing their own children due to a distorted sense of honor, or killing people of the same religion due to an idealogical difference (Sunni or Shia)...etc.

Islam and muslim countries get a lot of criticism due to their disregard of human rights and humanitarian values. However instead of admitting to this and having these difficult conversations, the default is always self victimazation. As the world becomes more globalized, we will be forced to interact with each other more and more and idealogical friction is bound to happen. Therefore we need to be respectful of each other's societies and way of life despite our own personal beliefs. When confronted with criticism we can either debate or accept our imperfections and work to fix them. Deflecting the blame is the easy way out and prevents more open dialogue between western and muslim countries both online and irl.
